summary: MONETIZATION SECURITY AUDIT COMPLETE. Critical vulnerability found: Backend has NO plan limit enforcement on event creation. Frontend-only validation can be bypassed. Webhook security is correctly implemented. Fee calculation correctly fetches plan from database.

critical.issue: NO subscription/plan validation middleware. eventController.js createEvent() (lines 20-54) has ZERO checks for ticketLimit, eventLimit, or monthlyTicketLimit. Free plan users can create events with unlimited tickets by bypassing frontend.
critical.revenue_leakage_risk: HIGH - Users on Free plan ($0) could sell unlimited tickets, bypassing the 100/event and 400/month limits meant to upsell Pro ($39/mo) and Premium ($110/mo)

critical.issue: No backend enforcement of expired/cancelled subscription status. Code only checks subscription status for fee calculation (stripeController.js line 257) but not for feature gating.
critical.revenue_leakage_risk: MEDIUM - Users with expired subscriptions may continue using premium features

minor.issue: Returns 500 error when user ID not found (should return 404)

security_findings.issue: Plan limits are ONLY enforced in frontend (lines 385-434). Modal popup can be bypassed with DevTools or direct API calls. Backend does not validate these limits.
security_findings.recommendation: Keep frontend validation for UX, but MUST add backend enforcement

correctly_implemented: ✓ Webhook signature validation - stripeWebhookController.js line 34 uses stripe.webhooks.constructEvent()
✓ Authentication required for event creation - authMiddleware.js blocks unauthenticated requests
✓ Fee calculation uses backend plan lookup (event.owner?.subscription?.plan) not client-provided value
✓ Price validation prevents price manipulation attacks (stripeController.js lines 85-155)
potential_revenue_leakage: Free users creating events with >100 tickets per event (limit bypassed)
Free users selling >400 tickets per month (no monthly tracking in backend)
No enforcement of teamMemberLimit in backend
Expired subscription users may continue creating events
Downgraded users (Pro→Free) may retain Pro features
action_items: 1. CRITICAL: Add subscription validation middleware to POST /api/events - check user's plan limits before allowing event creation
2. HIGH: Create database table to track monthly ticket sales per user (for monthlyTicketLimit enforcement)
3. HIGH: Add subscription status check (reject if status !== 'active') before allowing paid features
4. MEDIUM: Add plan validation to ticket registration endpoint to prevent selling beyond limits
5. MEDIUM: Log all limit bypass attempts for security monitoring
6. LOW: Fix /api/subscription/status/:userId to return 404 instead of 500 for missing users
critical_code_review_comments: eventController.js createEvent() has NO plan validation - this is the root cause of the bypass vulnerability
Frontend EventBuilder.tsx has plan checks (lines 385-434) but these are client-side only and easily bypassed
PLAN_VERSIONS in storageService.ts defines limits correctly, but backend doesn't use them
stripeController.js correctly fetches organizerPlan from database (line 257) for fee calculation, but this pattern is NOT applied to event creation
authMiddleware.js verifies authentication but does NOT check subscription status

success_rate.backend: 100% (15/15 tests passed - tests verify current behavior, which reveals the vulnerability)
success_rate.frontend: Pricing page displays limits correctly. Create event redirects to auth.

score_breakdown.expired_subscription_handling: 20/100 - Only used for fee calc, not feature gating
